question.text: A square loop of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is placed vertically in the east-west plane. A uniform magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> is set up across the plane in the north-east direction. The magnetic field is decreased to zero in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> at a steady rate. Then, the magnitude of induced emf is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _______.

solution.text:
The area vector for the square loop is given by

A→=(0.1)2 j^ m2

According to the above diagram, the magnetic field is given by

B→=0.22i^+0.22j^

Hence, the magnitude of induced emf can be calculated as follows

e=ΔϕΔt=B→·A→-01=0.22i^+0.22j^·(0.1)2 j^ -01 V=2×10-3 V

Hence, x=2.
